text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM

- Mubarak tells French magazine in an interview that it would be very dangerous if Netanyahu continued to violate agreements and closed the door to negotiations. He says Arabs are more united against Israeli government policies, including settlements; adds that Assad does not trust Israelis and that it would be difficult to persuade Syria to negotiate now.
- Arafat in Cairo on Friday for talks with President Mubarak.
- Moussa says after delivering Mubarak message to Chirac that Israeli position has made the whole world pessimistic.
- Mubarak discusses regional issues in telephone conversations with Assad and Hussein.

- Cabinet issues decrees to protect consumers and attract investors -- body to be set up to organise electrical services and to protect consumers. Assigns 209 million pounds for Shubra Kheima-Giza metro line.
- U.S. ambassador says his country welcomes Mubarak visit but leaves date up to president.
- Mahdi blames Bashir regime for ruining relations between Egypt and Sudan.
- Finance minister says state thinking of reducing income tax.
- Foreign Ministry checks up on Egyptian ambassador in Peru.
AL-AKHBAR
- Cabinet meeting headed by Prime Minister Ganzouri says Egypt rejects all kinds of Israeli settlement activity on occupied land.
- Mubarak tells French magazine that if things continue the way they are in the peace process there will never be understanding or stability in the region.
- Public prosecutor bars 92 housing officials from travelling for wasting public money on unfit buildings.
- Food and Agriculture Organisation says Egypt produced 5.7 million tonnes of wheat this year.
- Campaign to protect market from smuggled textiles and clothes.
- Plane ticket prices to increase in January.
AL-GOMHURIA
- Finance minister says ministry thinking of replacing sales tax with value added tax in a bid to safeguard investment.
